notes: Comprehensive component-by-component comparison of all 63 Java source files under src/main/java/org/apache/commons/validator against the Python working copy under src/main/org/apache/commons/validator. Findings: (1) Every Java module/class has a 1:1 Python module counterpart at the same relative path (org/apache/commons/validator/**), matching the AlphaTrans skeleton's package layout. (2) Method-level census: for every class, per-file method counts were compared (`def` in Python vs Java method signatures) -- Python counts are always >= Java counts (equal for simple classes, higher where private helper functions or dunder methods such as __str__/__eq__ were added per the brief's idiomatic-Python guidance), and spot checks (ValidatorResources, Form, FormSet, ValidatorAction, Validator, GenericValidator, GenericTypeValidator, DomainValidator) confirmed every individual Java method name/overload has a matching Python method (including numeric-suffix-disambiguated overloads like isValid0/isValid1/isValid2, isInRange0..5, formatByte0/1, etc.). (3) Grep for stub markers (`pass`-only bodies, `NotImplementedError`, `TODO`, `...`) found only legitimate, non-gap occurrences: no-op `__init__` constructors that mirror empty Java constructors (e.g. IBANCheckDigit, DateValidator, EmailValidator, ISBNValidator wrapper class, CreditCardValidator wrapper), an exception placeholder class body (`_URISyntaxException` in UrlValidator.py, a local Python stand-in for java.net.URISyntaxException), and abstract/interface method declarations that mirror Java abstract methods and ARE overridden by every concrete subclass -- verified concretely: CreditCardType.matches (Java interface method) is implemented in all four subclasses Amex/Visa/Mastercard/Discover; CheckDigit.isValid/calculate (Java interface) implemented in every concrete check-digit class; ModulusCheckDigit._weightedValue (Java abstract method) implemented in all 8 concrete subclasses (ABANumberCheckDigit, CUSIPCheckDigit, EAN13CheckDigit, ISBN10CheckDigit, ISINCheckDigit, ISSNCheckDigit, LuhnCheckDigit, ModulusTenCheckDigit, SedolCheckDigit); AbstractFormatValidator._getFormat/_processParsedValue/isValid3 (Java abstract methods) implemented in AbstractCalendarValidator/AbstractNumberValidator and their concrete subclasses (Byte/Short/Integer/Long/Float/Double/BigDecimal/BigInteger/Currency/Percent/Date/Calendar/TimeValidator); PercentValidator and CurrencyValidator correctly omit their own _processParsedValue because in the Java source both simply `extends BigDecimalValidator` and inherit it unchanged. (4) Note on apparent size discrepancies: some classes (e.g. ValidatorResources.java 331 lines vs .py 88 lines) look smaller in Python, but this is because the *provided* Java source under cleaned_final_projects_decomposed_tests already strips most method bodies down to Javadoc-only stubs for methods that depend on XML/Digester/SAXException machinery explicitly out of scope for this benchmark subject (verified by reading the full Java file: only the constructor, buildKey, buildLocale, and getLog have bodies in the Java source itself) -- the Python translation faithfully reproduces exactly that reduced, in-scope surface, so this is not a gap. (5) All src/main/**/*.py files parse without SyntaxError (ast.parse check across the whole tree), satisfying the M0/build_check bar. No class, field, or method in the (already-scoped) Java source was found without a faithful Python counterpart, and no stubbed/placeholder body remains for any concrete, non-abstract method that the Java source itself implements.
